We use the 1Password CLI for this purpose. Example: ```bash op run --env-file="./.env" -- pnpm --filter=shared run db:deploy ``` ### Editing default models and prices You can update the default AI models and prices by adding or updating an entry in `worker/src/constants/default-model-prices.json`. Please note that - prices are in USD - the list is ordered by ID, so make sure to keep this order and insert new models at the end of the list - the `updated_at` field must be updated with the current date in ISO 8601 format. Otherwise, the change will be ignored. ### Transition period until V3 release Until the V3 release, both the JSON record must be updated **and** a migration must be created to continue supporting self-hosted users. Note that the migration must updated both the `models` as well as the `prices` table accordingly. ## Updating the OpenAPI Specs & fern SDKs We maintain the API specifications manually to guarantee a high degree of understandability. If you made changes to the API, please update the respective `.yml` files in `fern/apis/...`. document.content:
> ### 🧑‍💻 We're hiring > > Langfuse is growing fast (we doubled the team in the last 6 months) - since January 2026 we're part of ClickHouse, we're hiring engineering hybrid across the EU. > We hire engineers who love open source and great developer experiences. > **[See open roles →](https://langfuse.com/careers?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=hiring&utm_content=langfuse)** # Contributing to Langfuse First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! ❤️ The best ways to contribute to Langfuse: - Submit and vote on [Ideas](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/categories/ideas) - Create and comment on [Issues](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues) - Open a PR. We welcome contributions through GitHub pull requests. This document outlines our conventions regarding development workflow, commit message formatting, contact points, and other resources. Our goal is to simplify the process and ensure that your contributions are easily accepted. We gratefully welcome improvements to documentation ([docs repo](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs)), the core application (this repo) and the SDKs ([Python](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-python), [JS](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-js)). The maintainers are available on [Discord](https://langfuse.com/discord) in case you have any questions. > And if you like the project, but just don't have time to contribute code, that's fine. There are other easy ways to support the project and show your appreciation, which we would also be very happy about: > > - Star the project; > - Tweet about it; > - Refer to this project in your project's readme; > - Submit and vote on [Ideas](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/categories/ideas); > - Create and comment on [Issues](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues); > - Mention the project at local meetups and tell your friends/colleagues. ## Making a change _Before making any significant changes, please [open an issue](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues)._ Discussing your proposed changes ahead of time will make the contribution process smooth for everyone. Changes that were not discussed in an issue may be rejected. Once we've discussed your changes and you've got your code ready, make sure that tests are passing and open your pull request. A good first step is to search for open [issues](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues). Issues are labeled, and some good issues to start with are labeled: [good first issue](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22). ## Project Overview We recommend checking out DeepWiki to familiarize yourself with the project: [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/langfuse/langfuse) ### Technologies we use - Application (this repository) - NextJS 14, pages router - NextAuth.js / Auth.js - tRPC: Frontend APIs - Prisma ORM - Zod v4 - Tailwind CSS - shadcn/ui tailwind components (using Radix and tanstack) - Fern: generate OpenAPI spec and Pydantic models - JS SDK ([langfuse/langfuse-js](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-js)) - openapi-typescript to generated types based on OpenAPI spec - Python SDK ([langfuse/langfuse-python](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-python)) - Pydantic for input validation, models generated by fern ### Architecture Overview See this [diagram](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting#architecture) for an overview of the architecture. ### Network Overview ```mermaid flowchart TB User["UI, API, SDKs"] subgraph vpc["VPC"] Web["Web Server
(langfuse/langfuse)"] Worker["Async Worker
(langfuse/worker)"] Postgres["Postgres - OLTP
(Transactional Data)"] Cache["Redis/Valkey
(Cache, Queue)"] Clickhouse["Clickhouse - OLAP
(Observability Data)"] S3["S3 / Blob Storage
(Raw events, multi-modal attachments)"] end LLM["LLM API/Gateway
(optional)"] User --> Web Web --> S3 Web --> Postgres Web --> Cache Web --> Clickhouse Web -.->|"optional for playground"| LLM Cache --> Worker Worker --> Clickhouse Worker --> Postgres Worker --> S3 Worker -.->|"optional for evals"| LLM ``` ### Database Overview The diagram below may not show all relationships if the foreign key is not defined in the database schema. For instance, `trace_id` in the `observation` table is not defined as a foreign key to the `trace` table to allow unordered ingestion of these objects, but it is still a foreign key in the application code. Full database schema: [packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma](packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma) ## Repository Structure We built a monorepo using [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/motivation) and [turbo](https://turbo.build/repo/docs) to manage the dependencies and build process. The monorepo contains the following packages: - `web`: is the main application package providing Frontend and Backend APIs for Langfuse. - `worker`: contains an application for asynchronous processing of tasks. - `packages`: - `shared`: contains shared code between the above packages. - `config-eslint`: contains eslint configurations which are shared between the above packages. - `config-typescript`: contains typescript configurations which are shared between the above packages. - `ee`: contains all enterprise features. See [EE README](ee/README.md) for more details. ## Development Setup Requirements - Node.js 24 as specified in the [.nvmrc](.nvmrc) - Pnpm v.11.10.0 - Docker to run the database locally - Clickhouse client **Note:** You can also simply run Langfuse in a **GitHub Codespace** via the provided devcontainer. To do this, click on the green "Code" button in the top right corner of the repository and select "Open with Codespaces". ### Codex Cloud Setup You can also attach this repository to an OpenAI Codex cloud environment. The cloud environment itself is configured in the Codex UI, while the repo-owned bootstrap is versioned in: - `scripts/codex/setup.sh` - `scripts/codex/maintenance.sh` Recommended Codex UI configuration: 1. Create a new cloud environment for this repository in the Codex UI. 2. Choose a base environment with Node.js 24 support. 3. Set the setup script to: ```bash bash scripts/codex/setup.sh ``` 4. Set the maintenance script to: ```bash bash scripts/codex/maintenance.sh ``` 5. Keep internet access disabled by default, or only allow the minimum domains needed for your task. 6. Add secrets and environment variables in the Codex UI instead of committing them to the repository. Notes: - This Codex setup is intended for repository tasks such as code changes, linting, typechecking, and targeted tests. - It does **not** start the full Langfuse stack. Local development still uses Docker and `pnpm run dx` / `pnpm run dev`. - Running the full application inside Codex requires external services for PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse, and object storage, plus matching environment variables in the Codex UI. ### Shared Agent Setup This repository keeps the shared agent setup in source control so developers using different tools can work against the same instructions, bootstrap, and MCP server catalog. - Canonical shared docs: - `.agents/AGENTS.md` - Root discovery symlinks: - `AGENTS.md` - `CLAUDE.md` - Shared agent setup overview: `.agents/README.md` - Shared skills: `.agents/skills/` - Shared tool/bootstrap/MCP config: `.agents/config.json` - Tool-specific MCP configs generated locally from that catalog and not committed: - `.mcp.json` - `.cursor/mcp.json` - `.vscode/mcp.json` - `.codex/config.toml` - Tool-specific runtime shims generated locally from the shared config and not committed: - `.claude/settings.json` - `.codex/environments/environment.toml` - `.cursor/environment.json` - Tool-specific skill projections generated locally and not committed: - `.claude/skills/*` - Shared bootstrap for agent environments: `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh` When you change the shared MCP setup: 1. Edit `.agents/config.json` 2. Run `pnpm run agents:sync` 3. Run `pnpm run agents:check` 4. Do not commit the generated MCP config files or runtime shims **Steps** 1. Install development dependencies: - [golang-migrate](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/tree/master/cmd/migrate#migrate-cli) as CLI - [clickhouse binary](https://clickhouse.com/docs/install) on macOS with brew: `curl https://clickhouse.com/ | sh` 2. Fork the repository and clone it locally ```bash git clone https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git cd langfuse ``` 3. Install dependencies and set up pre-commit hooks ```bash pnpm install pnpm run prepare # Sets up Husky pre-commit hooks for code formatting ``` The pre-commit hook runs formatting and lint checks. To skip only the lint check for a commit, set `LANGFUSE_PRE_COMMIT_SKIP_LINT`, for example: ```bash LANGFUSE_PRE_COMMIT_SKIP_LINT=1 git commit -m "your commit message" ``` CI still runs the required checks for pull requests. 4. Create an env file ```bash cp .env.dev.example .env ``` 5. Run the entire infrastructure in dev mode. **Note**: if you have an existing database, this command wipes it. Also, this will fail on the very first run. Please run it again. ```bash pnpm run dx # first run only (resets db, docker containers, etc...) pnpm run dev # any subsequent runs ``` You will be asked whether you want to reset Postgres and ClickHouse. Confirm both with 'Y' and press enter. 6. Open the web app in your browser to start using Langfuse: - [Sign up page, http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) - [Demo project, http://localhost:3000/project/7a88fb47-b4e2-43b8-a06c-a5ce950dc53a](http://localhost:3000/project/7a88fb47-b4e2-43b8-a06c-a5ce950dc53a) 7. Log in as a test user: - Username: `demo@langfuse.com` - Password: `password` To get comprehensive example data, you can use the `seed` command: ```sh pnpm run db:seed:examples ``` ## Monorepo quickstart - Available packages and their dependencies Packages are included in the monorepo according to the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file. Each package maintains its own dependencies defined in the `package.json`. Internal dependencies can be added as well by adding them to the package dependencies: `"@langfuse/shared": "workspace:*"`. - Executing commands You can run commands in all packages at once. For example, to install all dependencies in all packages, you can execute: ```bash pnpm install pnpm run dev pnpm --filter=web run dev # execute command only in one package pnpm tc # fast typecheck all packages pnpm build:check # Full Next.js build to alternate dir (can run parallel with dev server) ``` In the root `package.json`, you can find scripts which are executed with turbo e.g. `turbo run dev`. These scripts are executed with the help of Turbo. Turbo executes the commands in all packages taking care of the correct order of execution. Task definitions can be found in the `turbo.config.js` file. - Run migrations To run migrations, you can execute the following command. ```bash pnpm run db:migrate -- --name ``` > [!NOTE] > If you frequently switch branches, use `pnpm run dx` instead of `pnpm run dev`. This command will install dependencies, reset the database (wipe and apply all migrations), and run the database seeder with example data before starting the development server. > [!NOTE] > If you find yourself stuck and want to clean the repo, execute `pnpm run nuke`. It will remove all node_modules and build files. ## System behavior ### Ingestion API `(/public/api/ingestion)` - the ingestion API takes different event types (creation and updates of traces, generations, spans, events) - The API loops through each event and: - validates the event - stores the event raw in the events table - calculates tokens for `generations` - matches models from the `models` table to model for `generations` events - upserts the event in the `traces` or `observations` table - returns a `207` HTTP status code with a list of errors if any event failed to be ingested ## Commit messages On the main branch, we adhere to the best practices of [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/). All pull requests and branches are squash-merged to maintain a clean and readable history. This approach ensures the addition of a conventional commit message when merging contributions. ## Running Unit Tests All tests run in the CI and must pass before merging. All tests run against a running langfuse instance and **write/delete real data from the database**. ### Test Database Setup Per default, the tests use the local development database. Therefore, wiping your data in the process. For proper test isolation, create a `.env.test` file in the root directory: ```bash cp .env.test.example .env.test ``` Then, a different PostgreSQL and Redis are used for the tests. The `.env.test` file only overrides the set values and falls back on `.env` for all undefined values. - **PostgreSQL**: Uses separate `langfuse_test` database for isolation - **ClickHouse**: Uses shared `default` database for now - **Redis**: Uses database 1 instead of 0 for isolation (Redis data is not cleaned between tests) Tests automatically create the PostgreSQL test database if it doesn't exist and clean up data between runs. ### Tests in the `web` package (public API) We're using Vitest in the `web` package. There are two types of unit tests: - `test` (server tests) - `test-client` To run a specific test by name within a file, run: ```sh cd web # or use `pnpm --filter web test ...` from the repository root pnpm test prompts.v2.servertest -t "should handle special characters in prompt names" ``` To run all tests: ```sh pnpm run test ``` Run interactively in watch mode (not recommended!) ```sh pnpm run test:watch ``` ### Tests in the `worker` package For the `worker` package, we're also using Vitest to run unit tests. ```sh pnpm --filter worker run test FILE_YOU_WANT_TO_TEST.ts -t "test name" ``` ## CI/CD We use GitHub Actions for CI/CD, the configuration is in [`.github/workflows/pipeline.yml`](.github/workflows/pipeline.yml) CI on `main` and `pull_request` - Check Linting - E2E test of API using Vitest - E2E tests of UI using Playwright CD on `main` - Publish Docker image to GitHub Packages if CI passes. Done on every push to `main` branch. Only released versions are tagged with `latest`. ## Staging environment We run a staging environment at [https://staging.langfuse.com](https://staging.langfuse.com) that is automatically deployed on every push to `main` branch. The same environment is also used for preview deployments of pull requests. Limitations: - SSO is not available as dynamic domains are not supported by most SSO providers. - When making changes to the database, migrations to the staging database need to be applied manually by a maintainer. If you want to interactively test database changes in the staging environment, please reach out. You can use the staging environment end-to-end with the Langfuse integrations or SDKs (host: `https://staging.langfuse.com`). However, please note that the staging environment is not intended for production use and may be reset at any time. ## Production environment We run two separate release/deployment processes: 1. **Langfuse Cloud deployment (frequent):** - Every commit on the `production` branch triggers an ECS deployment to Langfuse Cloud. - To deploy current `main` to Langfuse Cloud, promote `main` to `production` via [`promote-main-to-production.yml`](.github/workflows/promote-main-to-production.yml) (instead of force pushing from a local machine). 2. **Open-source release (less frequent):** - The open-source Docker release process is handled via [`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) for self-hosted production users. You can trigger the Langfuse Cloud promotion in either way: 1. Preferred local command: ```bash pnpm run release:cloud ``` This wraps the GitHub CLI trigger and performs preflight checks (main branch/sync checks and migration diff checks against `production`) before dispatching the workflow. 2. GitHub UI: open **Actions** -> **Promote Main to Production** -> **Run workflow**, then set `confirm=promote`. ## Theming At Langfuse, we utilize CSS variables to manage our theme settings across the platform. Our approach leverages separate CSS variables for backgrounds (--background) and foregrounds (--foreground), fully adhering to the [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming) color conventions. The background suffix can be omitted if the variable is used for the background color of the component. We recommend using HSL values for these colors to enhance consistency and customization. There is no need to manually handle dark mode styling with "dark:" prefixes, as next-themes automatically manages the theme switching. We use the 1Password CLI for this purpose. Example: ```bash op run --env-file="./.env" -- pnpm --filter=shared run db:deploy ``` ### Editing default models and prices You can update the default AI models and prices by adding or updating an entry in `worker/src/constants/default-model-prices.json`. Any error logs from the metrics exporter or platform around 02:00-02:20?\\n\\nannie_support: Pasting customer timeline: they saw normal QPS until 02:07, then dashboards show flatlines. No API errors reported, just the graphs. I'll attach the support bundle they uploaded in the ticket.\\n\\npriya_oncall: I'm looking at the metrics stream. Can you dump a sample metric name/labels for redwood_inference_qps? I suspect the label change we rolled last night.\\n\\ncaleb_platform: quick sample from the exporter at 01:58 (pre-deploy):\\n```\\nredwood_inference_qps{model_id=\\\"gptx-4-mini\\\",instance=\\\"gpu-42\\\",region=\\\"us-west-2\\\"} 12.3\\n```\\nAnd from 02:12 (post-deploy):\\n```\\nredwood_inference_qps{model=\\\"gptx-4-mini\\\",instance=\\\"gpu-42\\\",region=\\\"us-west-2\\\"} 12.1\\n```\\nSo exporter rename: `model_id` -> `model`.\\n\\nlucy_sre: That'll break any dashboards that `by (model_id)` or use the `model_id` template var. Grafana will group by label that no longer exists -> panels show one series or nothing.\\n\\nmike_product: Do we know which dashboards/panels are impacted? Is this only Console per-model throughput or other things too?\\n\\ncaleb_platform: Initial sweep: Console per-model throughput, per-model latency sparklines, and the per-model cost breakdown panels. Anything that expects `model_id` label is affected. Cluster-level aggregates (no label) unaffected.\\n\\npriya_oncall: Quick mitigation options:\\n1) Re-add compatibility label at scrape time (metric_relabel_configs) to copy `model` -> `model_id` on the metrics pipeline, hotfixing dashboards without changing them.\\n2) Update Grafana queries/templating to use a neutral label (e.g., `label_replace` to coalesce `model` and `model_id` into `model_key`).\\nWhich is faster? 1 is fastest to restore user-facing dashboards.\\n\\ncaleb_platform: I'll prepare a hotfix to metrics pipeline to restore `model_id` for now. Patch: add in Prometheus remote write processing or exporter relabeling: \\n```yaml\\nmetric_relabel_configs:\\n  - source_labels: [model]\\n    target_label: model_id\\n    action: replace\\n```\\nDeploying to metrics staging first.\\n\\ndeploy-bot: deploy started for metrics-pipeline-hotfix #1593 at 2050001248 by caleb_platform\\n\\nlucy_sre: Also let's update dashboards to be tolerant long-term. Example Panel query we can switch to: \\n```\\nlabel_replace(redwood_inference_qps, \\\"model_key\\\", \\\"$1\\\", \\\"model\\\", \\\"(.+)\\\")\\n +\\nlabel_replace(redwood_inference_qps, \\\"model_key\\\", \\\"$1\\\", \\\"model_id\\\", \\\"(.+)\\\")\\n```\\nThen `sum by (model_key) (rate(redwood_inference_qps[5m]))`\\n\\nannie_support: Customer informed and flagged as P2. They asked for ETA to see graphs back.\\n\\ndeploy-bot: deploy completed at 2050001254, all metrics-pipeline instances reported healthy.\\n\\npriya_oncall: I can see the per-model series repopulating now. Grafana panels in console show normal lines again for the customer (checked their org).\\n\\nmike_product: Great. Root cause summary for ticket: exporter refactor renamed label `model_id` -> `model` without a compatibility layer; dashboards referenced `model_id` -> panels lost per-model grouping.\\n\\ncaleb_platform: Action items:\\n- (P0) Hotfix applied to metrics pipeline to copy `model` -> `model_id` (done).\\n- (P1) Update all Console dashboards to use `model_key` via label_replace and ship a universal dashboard patch (owner: caleb_platform).\\n- (P1) Add CI check for metric label renames on PRs and require compatibility shim.\\n- (P2) Postmortem and notify customers that saw impact.\\n\\nlucy_sre: Also forwarding to infra-metrics for a longer-term story: recording rule to normalize labels upstream so consumers don't need to chase exporter changes.\\n\\nannie_support: Customer replied: \\\"Thanks, graphs back, appreciate the quick fix.\\\" Closing the case once PM signs off on follow-ups. :white_check_mark:\\n\\nmike_product: I'll own the customer follow-up note and the PM side of the postmortem.\\n\\ncaleb_platform: Will open PRs to update dashboards and add the exporter compatibility test today.\\n\\npriya_oncall: Marking oncall resolved, will keep alert thresholds on watch for 24h.\\n\\nannie_support: Closing thread for internal discussion. document.title: 2050001234 urgent escalation console thruput rows zeroed after label shift
document.content:
{
  "channel": "support",
  "thread_ts": "2050001234",
  "first_message_ts": "2050001234",
  "last_message_ts": "2050001302",
  "participants": [
    "annie_support",
    "caleb_platform",
    "priya_oncall",
    "lucy_sre",
    "mike_product",
    "deploy-bot"
  ],
  "thread": "annie_support: Customer on Dedicated spotted all per-model throughput lines collapsed to 0 in Console (only overall cluster QPS shows). They filed an incident, says it started ~02:10 UTC after a deploy. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/example.png

caleb_platform: Got the screenshot, thanks. Any error logs from the metrics exporter or platform around 02:00-02:20?

annie_support: Pasting customer timeline: they saw normal QPS until 02:07, then dashboards show flatlines. No API errors reported, just the graphs. I'll attach the support bundle they uploaded in the ticket.

priya_oncall: I'm looking at the metrics stream. Can you dump a sample metric name/labels for redwood_inference_qps? I suspect the label change we rolled last night.

caleb_platform: quick sample from the exporter at 01:58 (pre-deploy):
```
redwood_inference_qps{model_id="gptx-4-mini",instance="gpu-42",region="us-west-2"} 12.3
```
And from 02:12 (post-deploy):
```
redwood_inference_qps{model="gptx-4-mini",instance="gpu-42",region="us-west-2"} 12.1
```
So exporter rename: `model_id` -> `model`.

lucy_sre: That'll break any dashboards that `by (model_id)` or use the `model_id` template var. Grafana will group by label that no longer exists -> panels show one series or nothing.

mike_product: Do we know which dashboards/panels are impacted? Is this only Console per-model throughput or other things too?

caleb_platform: Initial sweep: Console per-model throughput, per-model latency sparklines, and the per-model cost breakdown panels. Anything that expects `model_id` label is affected. Cluster-level aggregates (no label) unaffected.

priya_oncall: Quick mitigation options:
1) Re-add compatibility label at scrape time (metric_relabel_configs) to copy `model` -> `model_id` on the metrics pipeline, hotfixing dashboards without changing them.
2) Update Grafana queries/templating to use a neutral label (e.g., `label_replace` to coalesce `model` and `model_id` into `model_key`).
Which is faster? 1 is fastest to restore user-facing dashboards.

caleb_platform: I'll prepare a hotfix to metrics pipeline to restore `model_id` for now. Patch: add in Prometheus remote write processing or exporter relabeling: 
```yaml
metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [model]
    target_label: model_id
    action: replace
```
Deploying to metrics staging first.

deploy-bot: deploy started for metrics-pipeline-hotfix #1593 at 2050001248 by caleb_platform

lucy_sre: Also let's update dashboards to be tolerant long-term. Example Panel query we can switch to: 
```
label_replace(redwood_inference_qps, "model_key", "$1", "model", "(.+)")
 +
label_replace(redwood_inference_qps, "model_key", "$1", "model_id", "(.+)")
```
Then `sum by (model_key) (rate(redwood_inference_qps[5m]))`

annie_support: Customer informed and flagged as P2. They asked for ETA to see graphs back.

deploy-bot: deploy completed at 2050001254, all metrics-pipeline instances reported healthy.

priya_oncall: I can see the per-model series repopulating now. Grafana panels in console show normal lines again for the customer (checked their org).

mike_product: Great. Root cause summary for ticket: exporter refactor renamed label `model_id` -> `model` without a compatibility layer; dashboards referenced `model_id` -> panels lost per-model grouping.

caleb_platform: Action items:
- (P0) Hotfix applied to metrics pipeline to copy `model` -> `model_id` (done).
- (P1) Update all Console dashboards to use `model_key` via label_replace and ship a universal dashboard patch (owner: caleb_platform).
- (P1) Add CI check for metric label renames on PRs and require compatibility shim.
- (P2) Postmortem and notify customers that saw impact.

lucy_sre: Also forwarding to infra-metrics for a longer-term story: recording rule to normalize labels upstream so consumers don't need to chase exporter changes.

annie_support: Customer replied: "Thanks, graphs back, appreciate the quick fix." Closing the case once PM signs off on follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

mike_product: I'll own the customer follow-up note and the PM side of the postmortem.

caleb_platform: Will open PRs to update dashboards and add the exporter compatibility test today.

priya_oncall: Marking oncall resolved, will keep alert thresholds on watch for 24h.

annie_support: Closing thread for internal discussion. Will post postmortem link when ready. :eyes:",

    "thread"
  ],

}

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Operator Telemetry Convergence & Skill Roadmap (2026)\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"author\": \"Lena Martinez\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-26\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Ravi Shah\",\n    \"Maya Lopez\",\n    \"Tom Anders\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"operator-training\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"cost-optimization\",\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"roadmap\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-scenario-playbook-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/token-cost-attribution-and-explainable-trace-playbook-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Overview\\n\\nThis roadmap captures a 4-quarter program to converge platform telemetry, reduce noise and cost, standardize operator tooling, and run a phased skill uplift for platform operators. The program is scoped to the Platform Telemetry domain (ingestion, enrichment, dashboards, alerting, synthetic validation) and the Operator Surface (console, runbooks, preflight checks).\\n\\nGoals\\n\\n- Consolidate overlapping telemetry pipelines into a single Platform Telemetry Hub (PTH) to improve signal quality and lower ingestion costs by 25% by Q1 2027.\\n- Reduce actionable alert volume by 40% through smarter alert synthesis and SLI reweighting.\\n- Shorten mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for degradation incidents to < 5 minutes for P1s and < 15 minutes for P2s.\\n- Certify 80% of operators on the new Operator Skill Path (OSP) by end of program.\\n\\nScope and Non-Goals\\n\\nIn scope:\\n- Telemetry convergence for LLM serving stacks (batching, kv-cache, scheduler) and platform control plane.\\n- Dashboard and alert library standardization and ownership handoff.\\n- Operator training curriculum and certification.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n- Upstream model infra changes (model code or kernels).\\n- Billing/finance rework beyond token cost dashboards.\\n\\nPrinciples\\n\\n1. One source of truth: pipelines should feed PTH; downstream consumers should not maintain independent ingestion.\\n2. Signal over noise: prefer composite signals (SLOs, token burn rate, cold-start rate) to single noisy metrics.\\n3. Operator-first UX: dashboards and runbooks prioritized for oncall efficiency.\\n4. Iterative rollout with synthetic validation and game-day verification.\\n\\nHigh-level Timeline (by quarter)\\n\\n- Q2 2026 (Discovery & Pilot):\\n  - Audit existing telemetry owners and catalogs. Deliver telemetry dependency map.\\n  - Build PTH prototype with ingestion adapters for: serve-metrics, prefixcache-proxy, batching-router, tenant-credit-service.\\n  - Run two operator game-days using prototype dashboards.\\n\\n- Q3 2026 (Consolidation & Alert Baseline):\\n  - Migrate 50% of consumers to PTH.\\n  - Establish baseline alert volume and false positive rate per SLO.\\n  - Launch Alert Synthesis Engine (ASE) v0: groups related signals and suppresses duplicates.\\n  - Publish initial Operator Skill Path (OSP) curriculum: Fundamentals, Telemetry Forensics, Escalation Decision Canvas.\\n\\n- Q4 2026 (Optimization & Training):\\n  - Complete migration of core serving signals into PTH.\\n  - Implement cost-signal gating: tiered retention for low-value metrics. Target 18% ingestion reduction this quarter.\\n  - ASE v1 adds cost-aware ranking and context enrichment hooks for runbooks.\\n  - Run live cert exams for OSP Level 1.\\n\\n- Q1 2027 (Stabilize & Handback):\\n  - SLA bake-in and SLO contract signoffs with customer-success and product.\\n  - Finalize dashboard library and documented handback to service owners.\\n  - 80% operator certification target met; program enters steady-state training cadence.\\n\\nDeliverables and Success Metrics\\n\\n- Platform Telemetry Hub (PTH) deployed in prod (service name: platform-telemetry-hub).\\n- Dashboard library: 12 canonical dashboards (Latency, Token Cost, Cache Health, Prefetch Cohorts, Batch Efficiency, Tenant Credit Exposure, SLO Burn Overview).\\n- Alert Synthesis Engine (ASE) with configurable grouping and suppression rules.\\n- Operator Skill Path (OSP) with 3 certification levels and exam artifacts.\\n- Success metrics: ingestion cost down 25%, actionable alerts down 40%, MTTA < 5m for P1s, operator survey NPS >= +35 after training.\\n\\nInstrumentation Specification (required metrics)\\n\\nOperators and service owners must ensure the following metrics are emitted with these labels:\\n\\n- serve_request_latency_ms{service, model_variant, region, tenant} (histogram)\\n- token_consumption{tenant, request_type} (counter)\\n- kv_cache_hit_ratio{shard, model_variant} (gauge)\\n- batch_efficiency{pool_id, seq_len_bucket} (gauge)\\n- cold_start_rate{instance_type} (counter)\\n- operator_action_latency{operator_id, action} (timer)\\n\\nFor each metric include resource tags: cluster, AZ, build_sha, deploy_env.\\n\\nDashboard & Alerting Standards\\n\\n- Dashboards must:\\n  1) Use SLO-centric top-level panel.\\n  2) Surface correlated cost and latency panels side-by-side.\\n  3) Include pre-filtered time ranges: 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d.\\n\\n- Alert thresholds guidance (examples):\\n  - P1: serving_p99_latency > 1200ms for 3m AND token_consumption rate spike > 3x baseline => pager duty P1.\\n  - P2: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m => notify oncall with playbook link.\\n  - Cost alert: token_consumption for a tenant > 5x rolling 7d median and not explained by release tag => create ticket and notify billing-signal channel.\\n\\nSample ASE rule (YAML)\\n\\ncode:\\n  - name: p99-latency-spike-composite\\n    group_by: [service, region]\\n    conditions:\\n      - metric: serve_request_latency_ms_p99\\n        comparator: '>'\\n        threshold: 1200\\n        duration: 180s\\n      - metric: token_consumption_rate\\n        comparator: '>'\\n        threshold: '3 * baseline'\\n    actions:\\n      - notify: pd-oncall\\n      - attach-dashboard: dashboard-id:latency-slo\\n      - run-suppression: if correlated_cache_drop within 5m\\n\\nOperator Skill Path (OSP) outline\\n\\n- Level 0 (Observer): 1 hour course, dashboard walkthrough, intro runbook.\\n- Level 1 (Responder): 1 day lab, two simulated incidents, written exam.\\n- Level 2 (Diagnostician): 3 day deep-dive, ownership of a telemetry domain, live proctored incident.\\n\\nTraining and Certification Plan\\n\\n1. Q3 2026: Publish self-paced modules and host weekly office hours.\\n2. Q4 2026: Instructor-led labs and first cert run.\\n3. Q1 2027: Mentorship pairs; require shadowing two P1 incidents for Level 2.\\n4. Ongoing: Quarterly recertification via 2-hour practical exam.\\n\\nRollout & Migration Playbook (high level)\\n\\n1. Telemetry Audit: maintain a CSV of producers, consumers, and cardinality. (Owner: telemetry-platform)\\n2. Pilot consumer migration: pick two low-risk consumers (prefetch-lab, shadow-latency) and migrate to PTH.\\n3. Validation: run synthetic scenarios (cold-cache storm, token-burst) and compare alerts.\\n4. Bulk migration in waves with operator training scheduled between waves.\\n5. Handback: update service-level dashboard links and archive old pipelines.\\n\\nOwnership & RACI (text table)\\n\\n- Program Lead: Lena Martinez (engineering)\\n- Telemetry Platform: telemetry-platform (team)\\n- Operator Training: platform-ops-learning (team)\\n- Cost & Billing Signals: finance-ops (team)\\n- ASE Delivery: runtime-observability (team)\\n\\nRisks and Mitigations\\n\\n- Risk: Loss of legacy signals during migration. Mitigation: Dual-write for 4 weeks and automated reconciliation checks.\\n- Risk: Operators overwhelmed by retraining. Mitigation: Staggered cohorts and recorded sessions.\\n- Risk: Cost savings not realized. Mitigation: Quarterly cost reviews and retention tuning.\\n\\nGame-Day and Validation Recipes\\n\\n- Cold-Cache Storm: simulate 10x prefix cache miss rate for 30m, verify ASE groups related alerts and does not pageduty for known degradation pattern.\\n- Token Surge: synthetic tenant emits 10x token rate for 15m; verify cost alert, token attribution traces, and runbook activation.\\n\\nPost-Implementation Reviews\\n\\n- Schedule structured retrospectives after each migration wave. Use the following template:\\n  1) What happened (facts)\\n  2) What went well\\n  3) Where we were surprised\\n  4) Action items with owners and due dates\\n\\nRelated Artifacts and References\\n\\n- Telemetry dependency map (link to internal Confluence page)\\n- PTH design doc: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/platform-telemetry-hub-design-2026\\n- ASE design: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/alert-synthesis-engine-design-2026\\n- Operator Skill Path curriculum (drive link)\\n\\nNext steps (this week)\\n\\n- Run telemetry owner audit; populate the CSV (owner: telemetry-platform).\\n- Schedule two pilot migrations and two game-days (owner: program lead).\\n- Draft OSP Level 0 module and solicit SME reviewers (owner: platform-ops-learning).\\n\\nContact\\n\\nFor questions or to volunteer as a pilot consumer, ping Lena Martinez (@lena) or the telemetry-platform slack channel (#telemetry-platform).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_4a5f521dd19f40b3b9d680a1b7776280\"\n}",

document.title: Operator Telemetry Convergence & Skill Roadmap (2026)
document.content:
{
  "title": "Operator Telemetry Convergence & Skill Roadmap (2026)",
  "space": "eng-platform",
  "author": "Lena Martinez",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-03-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-26",
  "reviewers": [
    "Ravi Shah",
    "Maya Lopez",
    "Tom Anders"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "telemetry",
    "operator-training",
    "observability",
    "cost-optimization",
    "runbook",
    "roadmap"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-scenario-playbook-2026",
    "/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/token-cost-attribution-and-explainable-trace-playbook-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Overview

This roadmap captures a 4-quarter program to converge platform telemetry, reduce noise and cost, standardize operator tooling, and run a phased skill uplift for platform operators. The program is scoped to the Platform Telemetry domain (ingestion, enrichment, dashboards, alerting, synthetic validation) and the Operator Surface (console, runbooks, preflight checks).

Goals

- Consolidate overlapping telemetry pipelines into a single Platform Telemetry Hub (PTH) to improve signal quality and lower ingestion costs by 25% by Q1 2027.
- Reduce actionable alert volume by 40% through smarter alert synthesis and SLI reweighting.
- Shorten mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for degradation incidents to < 5 minutes for P1s and < 15 minutes for P2s.
- Certify 80% of operators on the new Operator Skill Path (OSP) by end of program.

Scope and Non-Goals

In scope:
- Telemetry convergence for LLM serving stacks (batching, kv-cache, scheduler) and platform control plane.
- Dashboard and alert library standardization and ownership handoff.
- Operator training curriculum and certification.

Out of scope:
- Upstream model infra changes (model code or kernels).
- Billing/finance rework beyond token cost dashboards.

Principles

1. One source of truth: pipelines should feed PTH; downstream consumers should not maintain independent ingestion.
2. Signal over noise: prefer composite signals (SLOs, token burn rate, cold-start rate) to single noisy metrics.
3. Operator-first UX: dashboards and runbooks prioritized for oncall efficiency.
4. Iterative rollout with synthetic validation and game-day verification.

High-level Timeline (by quarter)

- Q2 2026 (Discovery & Pilot):
  - Audit existing telemetry owners and catalogs. Deliver telemetry dependency map.
  - Build PTH prototype with ingestion adapters for: serve-metrics, prefixcache-proxy, batching-router, tenant-credit-service.
  - Run two operator game-days using prototype dashboards.

- Q3 2026 (Consolidation & Alert Baseline):
  - Migrate 50% of consumers to PTH.
  - Establish baseline alert volume and false positive rate per SLO.
  - Launch Alert Synthesis Engine (ASE) v0: groups related signals and suppresses duplicates.
  - Publish initial Operator Skill Path (OSP) curriculum: Fundamentals, Telemetry Forensics, Escalation Decision Canvas.

- Q4 2026 (Optimization & Training):
  - Complete migration of core serving signals into PTH.
  - Implement cost-signal gating: tiered retention for low-value metrics. Target 18% ingestion reduction this quarter.
  - ASE v1 adds cost-aware ranking and context enrichment hooks for runbooks.
  - Run live cert exams for OSP Level 1.

- Q1 2027 (Stabilize & Handback):
  - SLA bake-in and SLO contract signoffs with customer-success and product.
  - Finalize dashboard library and documented handback to service owners.
  - 80% operator certification target met; program enters steady-state training cadence.

Deliverables and Success Metrics

- Platform Telemetry Hub (PTH) deployed in prod (service name: platform-telemetry-hub).
- Dashboard library: 12 canonical dashboards (Latency, Token Cost, Cache Health, Prefetch Cohorts, Batch Efficiency, Tenant Credit Exposure, SLO Burn Overview).
- Alert Synthesis Engine (ASE) with configurable grouping and suppression rules.
- Operator Skill Path (OSP) with 3 certification levels and exam artifacts.
- Success metrics: ingestion cost down 25%, actionable alerts down 40%, MTTA < 5m for P1s, operator survey NPS >= +35 after training.

Instrumentation Specification (required metrics)

Operators and service owners must ensure the following metrics are emitted with these labels:

- serve_request_latency_ms{service, model_variant, region, tenant} (histogram)
- token_consumption{tenant, request_type} (counter)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio{shard, model_variant} (gauge)
- batch_efficiency{pool_id, seq_len_bucket} (gauge)
- cold_start_rate{instance_type} (counter)
- operator_action_latency{operator_id, action} (timer)

For each metric include resource tags: cluster, AZ, build_sha, deploy_env.

Dashboard & Alerting Standards

- Dashboards must:
  1) Use SLO-centric top-level panel.
  2) Surface correlated cost and latency panels side-by-side.
  3) Include pre-filtered time ranges: 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d.

- Alert thresholds guidance (examples):
  - P1: serving_p99_latency > 1200ms for 3m AND token_consumption rate spike > 3x baseline => pager duty P1.
  - P2: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m => notify oncall with playbook link.
  - Cost alert: token_consumption for a tenant > 5x rolling 7d median and not explained by release tag => create ticket and notify billing-signal channel.

Sample ASE rule (YAML)

code:
  - name: p99-latency-spike-composite
    group_by: [service, region]
    conditions:
      - metric: serve_request_latency_ms_p99
        comparator: '>'
        threshold: 1200
        duration: 180s
      - metric: token_consumption_rate
        comparator: '>'
        threshold: '3 * baseline'
    actions:
      - notify: pd-oncall
      - attach-dashboard: dashboard-id:latency-slo
      - run-suppression: if correlated_cache_drop within 5m

Operator Skill Path (OSP) outline

- Level 0 (Observer): 1 hour course, dashboard walkthrough, intro runbook.
- Level 1 (Responder): 1 day lab, two simulated incidents, written exam.
- Level 2 (Diagnostician): 3 day deep-dive, ownership of a telemetry domain, live proctored incident.

Training and Certification Plan

1. Q3 2026: Publish self-paced modules and host weekly office hours.
2. Q4 2026: Instructor-led labs and first cert run.
3. Q1 2027: Mentorship pairs; require shadowing two P1 incidents for Level 2.
4. Ongoing: Quarterly recertification via 2-hour practical exam.

Rollout & Migration Playbook (high level)

1. Telemetry Audit: maintain a CSV of producers, consumers, and cardinality. (Owner: telemetry-platform)
2. Pilot consumer migration: pick two low-risk consumers (prefetch-lab, shadow-latency) and migrate to PTH.
3. Validation: run synthetic scenarios (cold-cache storm, token-burst) and compare alerts.
4. Bulk migration in waves with operator training scheduled between waves.
5. Handback: update service-level dashboard links and archive old pipelines.

Ownership & RACI (text table)

- Program Lead: Lena Martinez (engineering)
- Telemetry Platform: telemetry-platform (team)
- Operator Training: platform-ops-learning (team)
- Cost & Billing Signals: finance-ops (team)
- ASE Delivery: runtime-observability (team)

Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Loss of legacy signals during migration. Mitigation: Dual-write for 4 weeks and automated reconciliation checks.
- Risk: Operators overwhelmed by retraining. Mitigation: Staggered cohorts and recorded sessions.
- Risk: Cost savings not realized. Mitigation: Quarterly cost reviews and retention tuning.

Game-Day and Validation Recipes

- Cold-Cache Storm: simulate 10x prefix cache miss rate for 30m, verify ASE groups related alerts and does not pageduty for known degradation pattern.
- Token Surge: synthetic tenant emits 10x token rate for 15m; verify cost alert, token attribution traces, and runbook activation.

Post-Implementation Reviews

- Schedule structured retrospectives after each migration wave. Use the following template:
  1) What happened (facts)
  2) What went well
  3) Where we were surprised
  4) Action items with owners and due dates

Related Artifacts and References

- Telemetry dependency map (link to internal Confluence page)
- PTH design doc: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/platform-telemetry-hub-design-2026
- ASE design: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/alert-synthesis-engine-design-2026
- Operator Skill Path curriculum (drive link)

Next steps (this week)

- Run telemetry owner audit; populate the CSV (owner: telemetry-platform).
- Schedule two pilot migrations and two game-days (owner: program lead).
- Draft OSP Level 0 module and solicit SME reviewers (owner: platform-ops-learning).

Contact

For questions or to volunteer as a pilot consumer, ping Lena Martinez (@lena) or the telemetry-platform slack channel (#telemetry-platform).

(matters for naming + versioning discipline)\\n\\nEthan Park: internal-only (Console + Optimize + billing hooks). but we\\u2019re treating it like an API contract: versioned, compat rules, etc.\\n\\nAllison Grant: got it. internal still needs strict compat. on naming: consistent `snake_case` is fine. what we should avoid is mixing synonyms (`input_tokens` vs `prefill_tokens`) unless they\\u2019re meaningfully different. standards doc prefers:\\n- \\u201csemantic names\\u201d over \\u201csource names\\u201d\\n- explicit units in field names for currency (e.g. `usd_micros`)\\n\\nAlso: please include a top-level `schema_version` field in every payload (even if service has negotiation).\\n\\nBenji Okafor: +1 on `usd_micros`. I noticed `total_cost` in the output structs \\u2014 can we rename to `total_cost_usd_micros` (or `total_cost_micros_usd` if we have a standard)? ambiguous \\u201ccost\\u201d is going to hurt when finance asks what unit.\\n\\nEthan Park: makes sense. I can update `cost_usd_micros` across breakdowns and keep the human-readable formatting in Console layer.\\n\\nJada Williams: reviewing now. question on naming vs taxonomy ADR: the PR uses `stage=prefill|decode`, but some fields are `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`. For Console we want breakdown rows that match terminology in UI (\\u201cprefill\\u201d/\\u201cdecode\\u201d). Can we standardize on `prefill_tokens` + `decode_tokens` in the breakdown object and keep `input/output` only as alias/derived?\\n\\nNadia Rahman: +1. in metering we already split prefill/decode for cache attribution and it\\u2019s more precise than input/output. `input_tokens` gets messy with tool calls + system prompts.\\n\\nLogan Wright: from telemetry side: we have counters called `tokens.prefill` and `tokens.decode` (post-normalization). I\\u2019d avoid `input_tokens` entirely in the canonical spec if we can.\\n\\nEthan Park: ok, I\\u2019ll swap to `prefill_tokens` / `decode_tokens` in the canonical output. we can still expose `total_tokens` for simple usage charts.\\n\\nThomas Baird: quick perf note: please be careful about field cardinality in \\u201cbreakdown by \\u2026\\u201d. I saw optional `breakdown_by: [\\\"model_version\\\", \\\"region\\\", \\\"quant_profile\\\"]` in the doc. can we hard-cap to a small known set + enforce max buckets? (Console is going to call this hot path.)\\n\\nEthan Park: yep. the schema package includes \\u201cbounds\\u201d in doc comments but not enforceable at type-level. We\\u2019ll enforce in service + guidelines. (There\\u2019s a separate PR for guardrails but I can add stronger language here.)\\n\\nKaitlyn Nguyen: deprecation policy: for schema, the safest rule is:\\n- v1: additive only\\n- never reuse field meaning\\n- if we must change semantics, add new field + bump schema minor + mark old field deprecated in docs\\n\\nIf this ends up being protobuf-backed anywhere later, also: never reuse tag numbers. even if we\\u2019re JSON today, we should write the policy as if proto constraints apply.\\n\\nAllison Grant: +1. also strongly recommend we add a short \\u201cCompatibility & Deprecation\\u201d section to the schema README:\\n- no rename/removal in v1\\n- deprecations must include: `deprecated_since`, `replacement`, and \\u201cremoval earliest\\u201d (even if it\\u2019s \\u201cnot before v2\\u201d)\\n\\nYou can just encode that as docstrings (not as runtime fields) to start.\\n\\nChloe Martin: Console side: we can work with docstring deprecation as long as the client library doesn\\u2019t break on unknown fields. Please confirm the generated types / deserialization are tolerant (ignore unknown fields).\\n\\nEthan Park: yep, client lib will ignore unknown fields + we\\u2019ll include schema version negotiation. (PR #28462 covers the client; this PR is just schemas/tests.)\\n\\nRafael Mendes: SRE nit: can we standardize error codes for schema mismatch? e.g. if Console sends unsupported `schema_version`. maybe not in this PR, but please ensure guidelines include something deterministic (so alerts can key off it).\\n\\nEthan Park: not in this PR but good call \\u2014 I\\u2019ll add a note to the API guidelines doc and track a follow-up.\\n\\nElliot Price: docs ask: where is the canonical place for field semantics? If schema package has README + comments, that\\u2019s good, but we should link it from the internal docs site and keep it in sync. please add \\u201cDO NOT COPY FIELDS INTO CONFLUENCE\\u201d warning, or we\\u2019ll fork definitions again.\\n\\nTalia Benson: timeline: can we land this by EOW? we\\u2019re trying to unblock ENG-4822 review + Console mock payloads.\\n\\nEthan Park: yes. action items from this thread:\\n- rename currency fields to `*_usd_micros`\\n- standardize tokens as `prefill_tokens` / `decode_tokens` (drop `input_tokens` naming)\\n- add explicit `schema_version` in top-level types\\n- add \\u201cCompatibility & Deprecation\\u201d section (additive-only v1, docstring deprecation metadata)\\n\\nWill push an update tonight and re-request review.\\n\\nAllison Grant: :thumbsup: once those are in, I\\u2019m good to approve.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: :thumbsup: same\\n\\nJada Williams: :thumbsup: works for Console\\n\\nLogan Wright: :+1: from telemetry side\\n\\nKaitlyn Nguyen: :+1: please tag me on the updated commit, I\\u2019ll do a quick pass on the deprecation wording\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_bda5fd8434594774ad119e061549a717\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "eng-platform",
  "thread_ts": "1768721444",
  "first_message_ts": "1768721444",
  "last_message_ts": "1768727312",
  "participants": [
    "Ethan Park",
    "Benji Okafor",
    "Kaitlyn Nguyen",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Jada Williams",
    "Logan Wright",
    "Nadia Rahman",
    "Thomas Baird",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Elliot Price",
    "Talia Benson",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "GitHub Bot"
  ],
  "messages": "Ethan Park: hey folks — looking for reviewers on the cost model schema PR. mostly types + docs + serialization tests.

PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/28451

Would love :eyes: from @Allison Grant (api standards) + @Jada Williams/@Chloe Martin (Console) + @Logan Wright/@Nadia Rahman (telemetry) + @Kaitlyn Nguyen (versioning/auth implications).

2 specific questions before I merge:
1) naming conventions: we’re using `snake_case` JSON keys in the schema docs + generated types. any objections / places where we should align with existing metering names?
2) deprecation policy: for v1, do we want an explicit “deprecated fields” mechanism (docs + lint) vs just “don’t remove/rename, only add”?

GitHub Bot: Ethan Park opened pull request #28451: "Add cost-model schema package v1"

Allison Grant: :eyes: taking a look now. quick q: are these meant to be public-facing JSON contracts or strictly internal? (matters for naming + versioning discipline)

Ethan Park: internal-only (Console + Optimize + billing hooks). but we’re treating it like an API contract: versioned, compat rules, etc.

Allison Grant: got it. internal still needs strict compat. on naming: consistent `snake_case` is fine. what we should avoid is mixing synonyms (`input_tokens` vs `prefill_tokens`) unless they’re meaningfully different. standards doc prefers:
- “semantic names” over “source names”
- explicit units in field names for currency (e.g. `usd_micros`)

Also: please include a top-level `schema_version` field in every payload (even if service has negotiation).

Benji Okafor: +1 on `usd_micros`. I noticed `total_cost` in the output structs — can we rename to `total_cost_usd_micros` (or `total_cost_micros_usd` if we have a standard)? ambiguous “cost” is going to hurt when finance asks what unit.

Ethan Park: makes sense. I can update `cost_usd_micros` across breakdowns and keep the human-readable formatting in Console layer.

Jada Williams: reviewing now. question on naming vs taxonomy ADR: the PR uses `stage=prefill|decode`, but some fields are `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`. For Console we want breakdown rows that match terminology in UI (“prefill”/“decode”). Can we standardize on `prefill_tokens` + `decode_tokens` in the breakdown object and keep `input/output` only as alias/derived?

Nadia Rahman: +1. in metering we already split prefill/decode for cache attribution and it’s more precise than input/output. `input_tokens` gets messy with tool calls + system prompts.

Logan Wright: from telemetry side: we have counters called `tokens.prefill` and `tokens.decode` (post-normalization). I’d avoid `input_tokens` entirely in the canonical spec if we can.

Ethan Park: ok, I’ll swap to `prefill_tokens` / `decode_tokens` in the canonical output. we can still expose `total_tokens` for simple usage charts.

Thomas Baird: quick perf note: please be careful about field cardinality in “breakdown by …”. I saw optional `breakdown_by: ["model_version", "region", "quant_profile"]` in the doc. can we hard-cap to a small known set + enforce max buckets? (Console is going to call this hot path.)

Ethan Park: yep. the schema package includes “bounds” in doc comments but not enforceable at type-level. We’ll enforce in service + guidelines. (There’s a separate PR for guardrails but I can add stronger language here.)

Kaitlyn Nguyen: deprecation policy: for schema, the safest rule is:
- v1: additive only
- never reuse field meaning
- if we must change semantics, add new field + bump schema minor + mark old field deprecated in docs

If this ends up being protobuf-backed anywhere later, also: never reuse tag numbers. even if we’re JSON today, we should write the policy as if proto constraints apply.

Allison Grant: +1. also strongly recommend we add a short “Compatibility & Deprecation” section to the schema README:
- no rename/removal in v1
- deprecations must include: `deprecated_since`, `replacement`, and “removal earliest” (even if it’s “not before v2”)

You can just encode that as docstrings (not as runtime fields) to start.

Chloe Martin: Console side: we can work with docstring deprecation as long as the client library doesn’t break on unknown fields. Please confirm the generated types / deserialization are tolerant (ignore unknown fields).

Ethan Park: yep, client lib will ignore unknown fields + we’ll include schema version negotiation. (PR #28462 covers the client; this PR is just schemas/tests.)

Rafael Mendes: SRE nit: can we standardize error codes for schema mismatch? e.g. if Console sends unsupported `schema_version`. maybe not in this PR, but please ensure guidelines include something deterministic (so alerts can key off it).

Ethan Park: not in this PR but good call — I’ll add a note to the API guidelines doc and track a follow-up.

Elliot Price: docs ask: where is the canonical place for field semantics? If schema package has README + comments, that’s good, but we should link it from the internal docs site and keep it in sync. please add “DO NOT COPY FIELDS INTO CONFLUENCE” warning, or we’ll fork definitions again.

Talia Benson: timeline: can we land this by EOW? we’re trying to unblock ENG-4822 review + Console mock payloads.

Ethan Park: yes. action items from this thread:
- rename currency fields to `*_usd_micros`
- standardize tokens as `prefill_tokens` / `decode_tokens` (drop `input_tokens` naming)
- add explicit `schema_version` in top-level types
- add “Compatibility & Deprecation” section (additive-only v1, docstring deprecation metadata)

Will push an update tonight and re-request review.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: once those are in, I’m good to approve.

Benji Okafor: :thumbsup: same

Jada Williams: :thumbsup: works for Console

Logan Wright: :+1: from telemetry side

Kaitlyn Nguyen: :+1: please tag me on the updated commit, I’ll do a quick pass on the deprecation wording",

  ],

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"new-hires\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1987654321\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1987654321\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1987654360\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"ravi\",\n    \"devex-bot\",\n    \"jen\",\n    \"ops-bot\",\n    \"mike\"\n  ],\n  \"text\": \"ravi: hi folks, accepted the org invite and can clone repos, but when i try to push a branch to my feature fork i get a 403 from the UI and `git push` shows: \\n```\\nremote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/feature/ravi-setup\\nTo https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git\\n ! [remote rejected] feature/ravi-setup -> feature/ravi-setup (protected branch hook declined)\\nerror: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git'\\n```\\nI'm on 2FA, verified work email, SSO authorized. any tips?\\n\\n[devex-bot]: GitHub Push Hook Event: push rejected for ravi. Check branch protection rules and required reviewers/CI status.\\n\\njen: welcome ravi! quick things: are you pushing to the upstream repo or to a fork? we require forks for external contributors and require PRs for protected branches.\\n\\nravi: pushing to upstream because the onboarding doc said to create a feature branch on the repo. not a fork.\\n\\nmike: the infra repo has a strict branch-protection policy: direct pushes to main and release/* branches are blocked; for feature/* we require at least one codeowner review and a passing CI check called `infra-ci`. if your branch name matched release/* it would be blocked. which branch name did you use?\\n\\nravi: feature/ravi-setup (copied from doc example). looks like the hook rejected it specifically as protected branch.\\n\\njen: can you run `gh auth status` and confirm you have the correct account, then `git remote -v` to show remotes? sometimes people have origin set to upstream which requires org membership perms to push.\\n\\nravi: `gh auth status` shows Authenticated to github.com as ravi-dev (user) via GitHub.com OAuth. `git remote -v` shows:\\n```\\norigin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (fetch)\\norigin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (push)\\n```\\nSo origin is upstream.\\n\\nmike: ah \\u2014 if you push directly to upstream we only allow pushes from users in the \\\"maintainers\\\" team for certain branches. For regular contributors (everyone else) the flow is: create a fork, push branch to your fork, open a PR from your fork -> upstream. That bypasses protected-branch push restrictions. The onboarding doc should probably be clearer.\\n\\nravi: ok, i can fork and push. question: is there a quick way to change my origin to my fork?\\n\\njen: yes \\u2014 after you fork on GH UI, you can run:\\n```\\ngit remote set-url origin git@github.com:ravi-dev/infra.git\\n# then git push -u origin feature/ravi-setup\\n```\\nIf you prefer HTTPS: `https://github.com/ravi-dev/infra.git`.\\n\\nravi: did the fork + push and opened a PR, but CI is failing on lint. curious why CI can't run for my PR. logs say `infra-ci` didn't trigger.\\n\\n[ops-bot]: CI policy: Only PRs from forked repos require a workflow whitelist. Please comment `@infra-ci allow` on the PR to request the workflow run, or add a small commit with `[ci run]` in the message.\\n\\nmike: on our org we block some Actions from running on external forks unless explicitly allowed. either comment `@infra-ci allow` like ops-bot said, or ask a maintainer to run the job.\\n\\nravi: commented `@infra-ci allow`. also added a tiny README tweak to satisfy the linter to iterate.\\n\\njen: one more FYI: if you prefer not to use forks for internal team work, ask to be added to `feature-contributors` team and we can open a temporary branch-permission for your user, but we generally prefer forks for auditability.\\n\\nravi: thanks everyone \\u2014 PR is open and CI started after the allow comment. appreciate the help and the welcome :wave:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"text\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_4ae8b9d4ba5a4003b3d1ca812544c86e\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "channel": "new-hires",
  "thread_ts": "1987654321",
  "first_message_ts": "1987654321",
  "last_message_ts": "1987654360",
  "participants": [
    "ravi",
    "devex-bot",
    "jen",
    "ops-bot",
    "mike"
  ],
  "text": "ravi: hi folks, accepted the org invite and can clone repos, but when i try to push a branch to my feature fork i get a 403 from the UI and `git push` shows: 
```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/feature/ravi-setup
To https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git
 ! [remote rejected] feature/ravi-setup -> feature/ravi-setup (protected branch hook declined)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git'
```
I'm on 2FA, verified work email, SSO authorized. any tips?

[devex-bot]: GitHub Push Hook Event: push rejected for ravi. Check branch protection rules and required reviewers/CI status.

jen: welcome ravi! quick things: are you pushing to the upstream repo or to a fork? we require forks for external contributors and require PRs for protected branches.

ravi: pushing to upstream because the onboarding doc said to create a feature branch on the repo. not a fork.

mike: the infra repo has a strict branch-protection policy: direct pushes to main and release/* branches are blocked; for feature/* we require at least one codeowner review and a passing CI check called `infra-ci`. if your branch name matched release/* it would be blocked. which branch name did you use?

ravi: feature/ravi-setup (copied from doc example). looks like the hook rejected it specifically as protected branch.

jen: can you run `gh auth status` and confirm you have the correct account, then `git remote -v` to show remotes? sometimes people have origin set to upstream which requires org membership perms to push.

ravi: `gh auth status` shows Authenticated to github.com as ravi-dev (user) via GitHub.com OAuth. `git remote -v` shows:
```
origin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (fetch)
origin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (push)
```
So origin is upstream.

mike: ah — if you push directly to upstream we only allow pushes from users in the "maintainers" team for certain branches. For regular contributors (everyone else) the flow is: create a fork, push branch to your fork, open a PR from your fork -> upstream. That bypasses protected-branch push restrictions. The onboarding doc should probably be clearer.

ravi: ok, i can fork and push. question: is there a quick way to change my origin to my fork?

jen: yes — after you fork on GH UI, you can run:
```
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:ravi-dev/infra.git
# then git push -u origin feature/ravi-setup
```
If you prefer HTTPS: `https://github.com/ravi-dev/infra.git`.

ravi: did the fork + push and opened a PR, but CI is failing on lint. curious why CI can't run for my PR. logs say `infra-ci` didn't trigger.

[ops-bot]: CI policy: Only PRs from forked repos require a workflow whitelist. Please comment `@infra-ci allow` on the PR to request the workflow run, or add a small commit with `[ci run]` in the message.

mike: on our org we block some Actions from running on external forks unless explicitly allowed. either comment `@infra-ci allow` like ops-bot said, or ask a maintainer to run the job.

ravi: commented `@infra-ci allow`. also added a tiny README tweak to satisfy the linter to iterate.

jen: one more FYI: if you prefer not to use forks for internal team work, ask to be added to `feature-contributors` team and we can open a temporary branch-permission for your user, but we generally prefer forks for auditability.

ravi: thanks everyone — PR is open and CI started after the allow comment. appreciate the help and the welcome :wave:",

    "text"
  ],

}

arguments.title: Platform & Console onboarding and upstream code-triage procedure
arguments.summary: For Senior Platform & Console engineers working across LiteLLM and Langfuse: provision core tools through the canonical least-privilege access ticket and validate access within the 8-business-hour target; keep production, secrets, customer data, protected branches, and maintainer workflows separately gated by auditable approval. Set up both repositories from their canonical contributor guides and validate scoped changes with repository tests plus synthetic end-to-end gateway/trace checks. Triage by subsystem owner, link an internal ticket before upstream activity, redact all Redwood/customer-sensitive context, use fork PRs, obtain owner review, and route vulnerabilities privately. Cross-repo changes require gateway, console, telemetry, compatibility/auth, and SRE/Security review as applicable. Validate schema compatibility, bounded cardinality, failure/rollback behavior, and reconciliation before rollout.

# Maya Desai — Senior Platform Engineer onboarding plan

Status: reviewed draft; personal branch only; access approvals remain pending.

## Role and boundaries

Maya joins Ethan Park's Platform & Console team as a Senior Platform Engineer, focused on the LiteLLM gateway and Langfuse operations console. Her initial remit is gateway policy, request validation/routing, telemetry propagation, and operator-console workflows. She may develop and review changes in local, test, and approved staging environments. She must not receive production, customer-data, secret-write, protected-branch, release, or upstream-maintainer privileges by implication of title.

The team owns inference gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and operator-facing console behavior. Runtime kernels/model code, billing policy, security policy, and telemetry-platform infrastructure remain with their respective owners; changes crossing those boundaries require their review.
